newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares slump at close, looking for support.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares slump at close, looking for support.

text.p: Chilean shares extended a string heavy losses closing sharply lower in light trade with the market seen struggling to find its support level, said traders.
"The bolsa may have a soft tone at the opening, but I doubt the IPSA (index) will go down to 104 points. It should stabilize at current levels," said one dealer.
The selective index ended down 1.83 percent at 106.37 points. The general index shed 1.1 percent to 5,129.39 points.
Turnover shrank to 6.6 billion pesos from 12.4 billion pesos Friday.
The low turnover reflected a drop-off in foreign buy orders which had fuelled the bolsa's New Year rally, said dealers.
"Demand has dried up in the U.S. There's no news here so we've gone back to the same negative pattern seen in December," said one broker.
Investors are now starting to look company fourth quarter earnings which are widely expected to be good except for the electricity sector, said dealers.
Some firms, like telecom CTC, have already publishedtheir earnings figures which must by law be released by the end of February.
Leading decliners included power generator Endesa which slumped on fears that its profits will be hurt this year's drought, said traaders.
Endesa's stock also affected by the fact Friday was the last day for registering for the firm's most recent dividend.
Other losers included forestry firm Masisa, down 4.08 percent at 200 pesos and drug-maker LabChile which shed 3.95 percent to 365 pesos.
Winners steel producer Cap, up 1.84 percent at 1,100 pesos and pension fund manager Cuprum which rose 1.47 percent at 6,900 pesos.
